Application of stacks in computer systems12B2. When we perform another operation, it will be added on top of the previous operation.

Application of stacks in computer systems13B3. If we press the “undo” button, the program will follow the last-in first-out mode of manipulation, which means taking our last operation from the undo stack and put it into the redo stack.
Application of stacks in computer systems14B4. If we press the “redo” button, the program will pop the last operation that we have undone from the redo stack and put it back into the undo stack.
Application of stacks in computer systems15B5. When we perform the next operation, the program will clear the redo stack.
Application of stacks in computer systems16BMoreover, we need to use stacks when a program calls its sub-program. Call stack (調用堆疊) is a stack stored in RAM and used to coordinate sub-programs.
Application of stacks in computer systems17BWhen we call a sub-program, its stack frame, which stores information such as return address, will be pushed into the call stack.
Application of stacks in computer systems18BWhen the sub-program has been executed, its stack frame will be popped. The following is the operating principle of a call stack.

Queues425.3Suppose that you are now waiting in a queue outside a newly opened restaurant. The restaurant has no table reservation system.Instead, it let diners enter sequentially using the first-come, first-served approach.
The concept and manipulation of queues43ASince you are the first diner in the queue, you can enter the restaurant first. This mode of manipulation is called First-In First-Out (FIFO).

The concept and manipulation of queues44AA queue is a data structure that adopts the above mode of manipulation. When you add a data item to a queue (enqueue), that data item will be added to the end of the queue.
The concept and manipulation of queues45AWhen you take a data item from the queue (dequeue), the removed item will be the one at the beginning of the queue, i.e. the first item that you have added.
Application of queues in computer systems46BQueues are widely applied in computer systems. For example, the order of printing documents is stored as a queue in the printer memory.

The concept and manipulation of circular queue65FTo solve this problem, we can simply reset the pointers. When a pointer reaches the end of the array, the next value of the pointer is reset to the index of the first item in the array. In this way, a circular queue is formed.

Linked Lists835.4A linked list is formed by many nodes. Each node stores its own data and a pointer, which stores the address of the next node. Nodes in the linked list are all connected by pointers.
The concept and manipulation of linked lists84ATo add a new node to or delete a node from the linked list, we simply need to modify the pointers of the nodes.

The concept and manipulation of linked lists85AStack and queue data structures only allow us to add data at their ends, while a linked list lets us insert new data in the middle of a row of data items. Therefore, a linked list is more flexible than the previous two data structures.

Application of linked lists in computer systems86BAfter a file system has been used for a long time, a lot of files are created, edited and deleted. Files are stored in storage devices in the form of separate fragments.A linked list is one of the data structures used in memory management. The computer system connects all fragments of a file using a linked list.
Application of linked lists in computer systems87BFile A connected by a linked list:

Differences between linked lists and arrays88CLinked lists and one-dimensional arrays have similar uses in that both can store a series of data. However, as mentioned in Module D of the Compulsory Part, an array can store the same type of data only. On the contrary, a linked list can store different types of data.

Differences between linked lists and arrays89CMoreover, since an array stores data in a continuous memory, the computer can use the index to calculate the memory address quickly and easily, and access a given item directly. This method of data access is called direct access (also known as random access).

The concept and manipulation of stacks9AA stack is a data structure that adopts the above mode of manipulation. When you add (push) a data item into a stack, the item will be added to the top of the stack.when you remove (pop) a data item from a stack, the removed item will be the one at the top of the stack.

Differences between linked lists and arrays90CSince a linked list connects nodes by pointers, data items do not need to be stored in a continuous memory, instead, they can be stored separately in different locations. When we need to access the data item at a given location, we can only search the list from the beginning and follow the pointers. This access method is called sequential access.

Differences between linked lists and arrays91CAlthough arrays are more convenient than linked lists in terms of data access, adding or deleting items in arrays is more complicated. For instance, if we need to add an item to an array, we must move the items after a given location backwards one by one.
Differences between linked lists and arrays92CIn addition, to delete an item, we need to move the items after a given location forwards one by one.
Differences between linked lists and arrays93COn the other hand, it is simpler to add or delete a node in a linked list. We only need to change the directions of the pointers.
